title: D0PA1 Canonical Log Schema v1
$comment: CLAUDE.md 'WHAT D0PA1 ADDS': 'canonical versioned log schema'. This is a NEW, forward-looking schema -- logs written BEFORE this schema existed (every file in logs/ as of Gate 0 A4) are NOT migrated into it and are NOT expected to conform. Those are described instead by manifest/data_manifest.csv (Gate 0 A4) and remain in their own original, historical formats. Nothing in this repository's existing pipeline (stage1_step4_vectors.py's sample/window_summary records, controls/null_input.py, etc.) writes through this schema yet -- it exists and is validated (schema/canonical_log_writer.py), but is not wired into any real capture loop by this task. The stimulus/ROI/action-class fields below exist because the client's task harness (delivered separately, under its own acceptance review) will eventually populate them -- this schema defines the SHAPE those fields must have; it does not define the action-class vocabulary itself, which is BLOCKED pending the client's D2 decision (CLAUDE.md 'BLOCKED' section) and therefore left as an open string here, not a fixed enum.

missingness_reason.description: Fixed enumerated vocabulary a missing value's reason MUST be drawn from -- never free text, so a downstream reader can group/count reasons reliably. Extend this list (bump the schema version if a real new reason is found) rather than allowing an open string -- an open string here would let 'missingness is logged, never dropped' quietly degrade into 'missingness is logged with whatever string the caller felt like writing'. v2 (D0PA1 D7 task) added no_prior_history: session_z/raw representations never need it (they never look outside their own session), but persistent_z's cross-session baseline is undefined for a session with no strictly-prior session to draw on -- a structurally different cause from zero_dispersion (prior sessions exist but their spread is ~0) or insufficient_samples (too few observations within an otherwise-valid window).

canonical_session_header.description: Written EXACTLY ONCE per session_id, before any canonical_observation record for that session -- this is where 'the wall-clock offset recorded once per session' (this task's timing invariant) actually lives. Every observation's monotonic timestamps (stimulus_onset/prediction_timestamp/action_timestamp) are only interpretable as real-world time relative to THIS record's wall_clock_utc/monotonic_reference pair.

subject_id.description: Required on every record this schema governs, including a session header, from the first observation onward -- even a single-subject study stamps this (D0PA1 hard constraint #7).

commit.description: Git commit hash of the code running this session -- see simulation/provenance.py's RunProvenance.git_commit_hash.

wall_clock_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp captured at session-open time.

monotonic_reference.description: The monotonic clock's own value (e.g. time.perf_counter()) at the SAME instant as wall_clock_utc -- the offset between the two is what makes every later monotonic timestamp in this session interpretable as wall-clock time.

canonical_observation.description: One row = one signal's reading at one point in time, optionally joined with whatever trial/prediction/action context is available. A record is written for EVERY observation attempt, whether or not the signal itself was successfully read -- missingness is a row with a reason, never an absent row.

subject_id.description: Required on EVERY observation from the first record, even with one subject (D0PA1 hard constraint #7) -- enforced by the writer, not left to caller discipline.

trial_id.description: Null until the client's task harness defines trial structure (BLOCKED, D2).

model_version.description: Null for every geometric signal (V_bf/V_es/V_jc/V_pd/etc. -- no trained model in this pipeline, CLAUDE.md). Exists for a future trained-model consumer of this schema, not populated by anything in this repository today.

stimulus_id.description: Null until the client's task harness exists (BLOCKED, D2) -- see schema $comment. Not computed or inferred by this writer.

stimulus_onset.description: Monotonic timestamp (same clock as monotonic_reference in this session's header). Null until the harness exists.

action_timestamp.description: Monotonic timestamp. Null until the harness exists.

action_class.description: OPEN STRING, deliberately not a fixed enum -- the action-class vocabulary is BLOCKED pending the client's D2 decision (CLAUDE.md 'BLOCKED' section: action classes, horizon, tie/rapid-succession handling). When the harness exists and an action occurs, ABANDON and NO_ACTION MUST be logged here as real string values -- never represented by leaving this field null or by omitting the row (CLAUDE.md D0PA1 hard constraint: 'these must be REAL CLASSES in the log, not absent rows or a null'). A null here means 'no action-class information available at all' (harness not wired yet), which is a different fact from 'the action class IS the no-action outcome' (which is the literal string "NO_ACTION").

signal.description: Which signal this row reports (e.g. 'v_es', 'v_pd', 'screen_orientation') -- required; a row always names what it's about even when the value itself is missing.

value.description: This signal's reading. Null exactly when missingness_flag is true.

confidence.description: Per-signal confidence, independent of missingness -- a present value can still carry low confidence (see modality_quality for the sensor-level counterpart).

modality_availability.description: Was the underlying sensing modality (camera, audio, etc.) available at all this cycle -- independent of whether THIS signal specifically produced a usable reading.

modality_quality.description: Sensor/tracking-level quality indicator for the modality this signal derives from (e.g. detection confidence, landmark presence) -- distinct from confidence, which is about the signal's own reading.

missingness_flag.description: true iff value is null. Enforced by the writer to always agree with value's presence -- never set independently by a caller.

missingness_reason.description: Required (one of the fixed enum) whenever missingness_flag is true; MUST be null when missingness_flag is false -- the writer enforces both directions, not just 'a reason must exist when missing'.

prediction_output.description: Null until a real prediction model exists downstream of this schema (BLOCKED on D2, see CLAUDE.md) -- defined now so a future consumer has a stable field name, not populated by anything in this repository today.

ground_truth_outcome.description: Null until the harness/action-logging exists. Same 'real class, not absent row' rule as action_class applies here once it is populated.
